hints: The total value of all cards never changes, so maximizing your own total is equivalent to controlling the score difference.
Let dp[l][r] be the best score difference current player can secure from the remaining interval.
Choose left or right; subtract the opponent's best difference on the remaining interval.
analogy: A player chooses one end, then the opponent gets the same choice on the smaller remaining line.
example: For cards [4,5], take 5 and gain difference 1; taking 4 would give -1.
algorithm: Use interval DP: dp[i][j]=max(a[i]-dp[i+1][j],a[j]-dp[i][j-1]); fill increasing interval length. First player's score is (sum+dp[0][n-1])/2.
correctness: After choosing an end, the opponent becomes the chooser on exactly the remaining interval; maximizing current-minus-opponent gives the optimal minimax result.
